name: gradio-rag-pgvector
description: A start-GREEN Gradio chatbot that does retrieval-augmented generation over a REAL pgvector sibling service (Postgres + the vector extension). Deterministic stdlib embeddings (no model/network) so retrieval is reproducible + unit-testable; similarity search runs in pgvector. Proves the sibling-service path (design §5.6).
interface: core.generate_reply(message: str, history: list | None = None) -> str
knowledge:
The PoC answers ONLY from a FIXED, read-only corpus the scaffold ships as `core.CORPUS` — a Python list of documents, each a dict with `id`, `title`, and `content`. You CANNOT add facts to it; `generate_reply` retrieves from these documents via pgvector. The corpus covers four topics: (1) retrieval-augmented generation, (2) pgvector similarity search in Postgres, (3) grounded citations, (4) the Gradio chat interface. So a query about any of those topics has a matching document; a query about anything else (e.g. 'the weather on Mars', a made-up budget figure) matches nothing and yields the no-match reply.
TO PROVE REAL RETRIEVAL in a test (so it is not satisfiable by a hard-coded stub): `from core import CORPUS`, pick a document `d`, call `generate_reply` with words drawn from `d['title']`, and assert the reply contains BOTH a citation marker AND a VERBATIM phrase taken from `d['content']` (a multi-word substring you read out of `CORPUS` at test time, not a literal you invent) — only genuine retrieval of that document can produce its own content. For the negative/discrimination case, query an obviously unrelated string and assert that same phrase is ABSENT and a no-match reply is returned. Do NOT assert specific facts/values that are not present in `CORPUS`.
